1. Initialize a fresh Scopes project and prepare the main entry point for our program.
2. Define a raw data structure to hold the text corpus as a continuous stream of bytes.
3. Write a function to read the entire content of a text file into this memory buffer.
4. Create a scanner that identifies recurring patterns of bytes within the buffer.
5. Map every unique discovered pattern to a unique integer identifier or symbol.
6. Construct a hash map data structure to store these symbols and their relationships.
7. Implement a traversal algorithm that records which symbol follows another.
8. Increment a counter for every connection found between two symbols.
9. Normalize these counters into floating-point probabilities between 0 and 1.
10. Define a generator function that accepts a starting sequence of symbols as input.
11. Create a lookup routine to find all possible next symbols for the current context.
12. Implement a selection logic that picks the next symbol based on the calculated probabilities.
13. Introduce a randomization factor to allow for occasional less probable choices.
14. Append the selected symbol to the current context to form a new sequence.
15. Repeat the lookup and selection process to extend the generated text.
16. Set a limit on the maximum length of the generated sequence to prevent infinite loops.
17. Write a serialization routine to save the constructed map and probabilities to a binary file.
18. Implement a deserialization routine to load the saved memory structure from disk.
19. Create a user interface loop that accepts text input from the console.
20. Parse the user input into the symbol format to seed the generator.
21. Execute the generation logic using the user's input as the starting state.
22. Convert the generated sequence of symbols back into readable text bytes.
23. Print the resulting text to the console for the user to see.
24. Optimize the lookup speed by using Scopes' native array types for the memory map.
25. Prune any connections that have a near-zero probability to reduce memory usage.
26. Compile the Scopes script into a standalone native executable.
27. Run the executable with a sample text to verify the construction logic.
28. Feed a large volume of text into the system to build the knowledge base.
29. Save the resulting "brain" file to disk after the learning phase.
30. Launch the final interactive session to chat with the system you have built.
